ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left panel in the diagram is labeled “Producers and Consumers”; at the bottom there are plant producers Aromatic Sumac and Pigeon Berry; in the middle and upper parts there are consumers such as Brush Mouse, Field Cricket, Great Plains Toad, Eastern Cottontail, Rock Squirrel, Brown Snake, Barn Owl, and Gray Fox. Arrows connect different organisms, indicating that food or energy flows from the organism being eaten to the organism that eats it. Gray Fox is located in the upper left, and there are arrows from prey such as Brush Mouse pointing toward it; the diagram does not show Gray Fox being preyed on again by other consumers. The right panel is “Decomposers,” including Bacteria, Fungi, and Worms. Reasoning: The organism at the highest position in a food chain is usually the apex consumer that is not preyed on by other consumers. According to the direction of the arrows in the diagram, Gray Fox receives energy arrows from prey, and no arrows show that it is eaten by other consumers, so it is the organism at the highest food-chain position in the diagram.
